rationale: Replacing the rent level with its 3-year TS_MIN is a cosmetic variant of the already-tested "Joint Rent-Deleveraging Quality" (margins are highly persistent, so the rank of the 3-year minimum will be nearly collinear with the rank of the level), offering no substantively new economic mechanism.

The stability screen is a defensible, diagnosis-driven refinement of the prior term-match signal's sign disagreement (acquisition-driven intangible bursts in the long tail), though stacking three MIN-ranks risks a thin, unstable long leg and the identifiable-intangible leg alone may drive most variation.

This is essentially the sign-flipped, positively-weighted version of the previously tested debt-minus-equity financing-spread family (Intangible Risk-Capital Mismatch / Contractibility Capital Mismatch) with the intangible leg swapped for a rent margin, and because RANK is strictly positive the construction reduces to a rescaled net-equity-issuance signal — a well-known published anomaly.

This is a single-theme bounded transform rather than a genuine cross-theme interaction, and mechanically it ranks low-leverage, intangible-intensive firms highest, making it largely a repackaging of the known low-leverage and intangible-intensity effects.

The signed-change-times-signed-change "alignment" structure duplicates the already-failed Lifecycle Financing-Drift Mismatch with maturity mix substituted for financing source, and the symmetric prediction (shortening maturity while R&D falls is also good news) is economically unmotivated while the product of two noisy annual differences will have almost no reliable cross-sectional spread.

Converting the null-result Advertising Duration Match from MUL to MIN-of-ranks is a mechanical restatement already used repeatedly in this archive, and the underlying claim that short-maturity debt is favorable for advertising-intensive firms remains theoretically weak and contradicts the R&D-duration result in the same archive.
